themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key. There is no stable number to grade your work against, and the thing being measured often shifts while you measure it, so the models start by building a small truth set of their own or admit the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: Answer engine optimization answers call model drift larger than any brand action, incrementality answers say platforms change the treatment mid-test, identity resolution answers say no one has a truth set for who is who, B2B buying-group answers say a dead signal and a fake one look identical, and ad supply integrity answers say fake engagement is cheaper to make than to verify.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what will happen next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: All three models answer safe agent execution with a proxy, gateway, or control plane in front of every write, with blast-radius caps, dry runs, and shadow mode, and the same single-checkpoint move appears in the downstream consent answers (one gate on every data egress path) and in journey orchestration (one shared contact log every channel must check).

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Several problems stall because the party holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. The blocker is money and politics, inside the company as well as outside, so the models try to make honesty or cooperation pay instead of writing another rule.
themes.evidence: Agentic traffic answers all say agents profit by posing as humans and propose a fast lane with perks for those that declare themselves, the shared context layer answers call conflicting definitions of customer a political settlement rather than a modeling gap, and journey orchestration answers say channel owners paid on their own conversions will subvert any central arbiter.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch behavior from outside and estimate whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: Consent and deletion answers describe ad platforms and agency segments as black boxes with no test for removal from an already-trained model, and today's agent execution answers add that vendors expose no staging, reservation, or undo primitives, so safety has to be simulated from outside the system that owns the action.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning, context, and what counts as a good outcome, and no rule set captures that fully. So the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box rather than trying to remove it.
themes.evidence: Generative content governance answers converge on an approved-claims library because deciding whether wording is substantiated is a contextual judgment reviewers themselves dispute, the shared context layer answers argue two teams can both be right about what revenue means, and journey orchestration answers say no single metric compares a sale against customer harm.
